niche: a public servants' savings and credit cooperative forecasting how many of the first payroll-deduction loans it disburses to members employed by private firms will be in default a year later, from ten years of payroll loans to public-servant members and the monthly payroll registers the private employers send under their deduction agreements
answer: about 250 of the 2,400 loans in default by 31 January 2028 (247.0 expected); sector shares 20, 10, 10, 10, 10 and 5 per cent
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every file correctly, takes each public loan's default within twelve months of disbursement, fits a PD model on the borrower attributes (age, salary, tenure, contract type, instalment and term) and scores the 2,400 launch loans files about 50 in default by 31 January 2028, where the answer is about 250.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the launch loans' first-year probability of default, which payroll-deduction lending reads as the chance the borrower leaves the paying employer while the loan is open times the share of such loans that then default, the leaving rate taken from each employer's own payroll and the conversion from the public book; with patients, students or customers in place of borrowers the call loses the deduction at source that makes leaving the payroll the route to default.
layer1: the loan book carried from the legacy core (loans to June 2021, amounts in thousands of pesos, contract type as a letter) into the new core under new loan numbers with a crosswalk
the national treasury's monthly deduction returns listing only the loan-months not applied, under a coarse two-code scheme and a 2023 layout change, re-sent months duplicated

the private employers' monthly payroll registers sent under their deduction agreements since 2025, fortnightly and monthly payers side by side, mid-year and December bonus registers, vacation and final-settlement lines, re-sent registers and a payee-key change when the cooperative's intake portal was upgraded
the launch file of pre-approved applications with the employer's tenure certificate dates and the employer agreements register
the default register with 90-days-past-due entry dates, cures and re-entries
stakeholder_role: the cooperative's finance manager, who books the 2027 budget's loan-loss provision for the first private-employer loans from their first-year default forecast

spine.entity: one payroll-deduction loan disbursed to a public servant (or, for the legacy core, one loan as migrated)

world.org_type: public servants' savings and credit cooperative, payroll-deduction lending (fictional)

driver: A unit reaches the outcome almost only through one event, leaving the body that collects its payments while its obligation is still open, so its rate over a window is that event's rate times the share of such events that convert; the record's units leave rarely, and the ones that leave often hold obligations set to end before they go, so a model of the outcome on the units' own attributes reads the rarity of the event as their quality, while the forward units belong to bodies whose own payment records show them leaving several times as often.
driver_concrete: A payroll-deduction loan defaults almost only when its borrower leaves the employer's payroll while the loan is open, about 55 in 100 such loans reaching 90 days past due within months, so the public-servant book's first-year default of under 2 per cent is the rarity of permanent staff leaving, temporaries' loans being capped to end before their contracts; the private employers' own monthly payroll registers show their staff leaving five to six times as often, so about 250 of the 2,400 launch loans default by 31 January 2028, not the 50 a PD model on borrower attributes scores.
stump: A PD model fitted on the public book's borrower attributes and scored on the launch file gives about 50 of the 2,400 loans in default by 31 January 2028; the public book's defaults run almost wholly through borrowers leaving the payroll with the loan open, which the private employers' payroll registers show five to six times as often, so the count is about 250.

differentiation.task75: task75 adds a second arrival channel found as the residual between two internal counts and timed by a recurrence; here nothing is missing from any count: the default rate is read per exit from the employer's payroll with the loan open, and each forward employer's own payroll registers give how often its staff leave.
differentiation.task45: task45 nets a serviceable share of a contracted scope against a holding position rebuilt from a movement ledger; here the share built behind the join is how many launch loans' borrowers leave their employer's payroll while the loan is open, priced at the default rate the public book shows per such exit.
differentiation.task177: v2 conditioned a randomised offer's effect on the days to each subscriber's next bill; v3 has no test and no timing within a cycle: a default rate is read per payroll exit and carried to borrowers whose employers' payroll registers show exits five to six times as often.

lineage.niche: a provincial employment service's forecast of the share of jobseekers' own contacts its upgraded digital assistant takes in the eight weeks after an assistant-first period, from each claimant's contact-by-contact channel choices and the outcomes they met
lineage.driver: Experiences a unit did not choose move its later choices far less than experiences it chose, so a period that sends every unit to one option converts few of them; the record holds those imposed experiences only as scattered single episodes, so a learner fitted to the whole record with one rate over-predicts the conversion, and only a separate rate for the imposed experiences, read from those episodes, carries to the period.
lineage.driver_concrete: Jobseekers sent to the digital assistant when the phone queue overflows learn about a fifth as much from it as those who open it themselves, so the eight assistant-first weeks, which send every call to the assistant, lift claimants' own use of it in March and April far less than a reinforcement-learning model with one learning rate predicts.
lineage.stump: One learning rate fitted to every contact and simulated through the assistant-first weeks files about 40 per cent of claimants' own contacts in the assistant for March and April; the overflow-redirected contacts in the record teach about a fifth as much as chosen ones, so the share is about 26 per cent.
lineage.answer: 25 per cent (to the nearest 5 per cent; 25.21 unrounded)
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 Gate F on target.zip 3be16ba3 (2026-10-21): the re-judge was DETERMINISTIC and APPROVE, but scored reader I landed the 25 bin with a fitted outcome-weighted habit model (decay 0.63 per contact, weights by the previous contact outcome) that never separated the imposed contacts; whole per cent had failed determinism and nearest 5 admitted the neighbour, so the lever was no wider than the golden family spread

lineage.niche: a UK news publisher's forecast of the share of its January at-risk list of monthly digital subscribers that a half-price retention offer keeps through March, carried from last January's half-and-half test after billing moved to the 1st of the month
lineage.driver: An intervention moves a unit mainly when it lands in the days before the unit's own recurring decision, so the effect a randomised test measured while those decisions fell at every point of the units' cycles is an average over the cycle, and it does not carry to a delivery that now lands a few days before every unit's decision; only the effect the test read on its units whose decision fell as close to their delivery does.
lineage.driver_concrete: A half-price retention offer keeps a subscriber mainly when it lands in the fortnight before their next monthly bill, so last January's half-and-half test, sent while bills fell on every day of the month, kept about 9 in 100 across the cycle, while this January's list, every bill on 1 February six days after the send since billing moved to the 1st, is kept at the rate the test measured on subscribers billed within two weeks of it, about 20 in 100.
lineage.stump: An uplift model on last January's half-and-half test (two-model or transformed outcome on the subscriber features) scored on this year's list files about 10 per cent; the test's subscribers whose next bill fell within two weeks of the send were kept at about twice the overall rate and almost none of the rest, and every bill on this year's list falls six days after the send, so the share is about 20 per cent.
